TC-APT-096.blocking_reason: Direct reproduction on the PRE-FIX code confirmed the plan's self-deadlock diagnosis: store()/batch_store() caught lmdb.MapFullError INSIDE the still-open outer write transaction and opened a second write transaction there; on this platform/lmdb build that raised InvalidParameterError from set_mapsize() itself (LMDB forbids resizing while any transaction in this process is open), then BadTxnError unwinding the outer transaction -- a hard crash, not the graceful resize-and-retry the removed code's comments claimed. Fix: new _run_txn_with_map_recovery(txn_fn, max_attempts=3) wraps every call site whose transaction does not outlive the call (exact_lookup, store, batch_store, delete, delete_namespace, count, clear, export_all, count_by_config_fingerprint, lineage_index_stats) -- on MapFullError it grows the map (bounded by new named constant _MAX_MAP_SIZE_MB=8192, replacing the two inline `8192` literals) and retries the ENTIRE txn_fn fresh only after the failing transaction has fully exited its `with` block; LMDB transactions have no partial commit, so full-function retry is the only safe retry unit -- confirmed no double-write/double-count risk in delete_namespace (delete of an already-deleted key is a no-op) or batch_store (redo-whole-batch). Also fixed a previously-uncaught class: zero call sites anywhere handled lmdb.MapResizedError (MDB_MAP_RESIZED), so a sibling K-lane process resizing the shared LMDB file first would crash every OTHER lane's very next TM read or write; now recovered via env.set_mapsize(0) (adopt the sibling's new on-disk size) and retry. TC-APT-106.title: m2m100_418m real 25-locale quality assessment on real content: 3 concrete bugs found and fixed (table-placeholder identity collision, frontmatter placement-check stale-snapshot race, wasted deterministic-retry attempts)
TC-APT-106.note: Originated from an operator request to actually run m2m100_418m against all 25 mission locales on real GPU hardware, against real aspose.org content, to assess whether it is capable/good enough to be primary for more than the current 3 locales (hu/ja/ro). Built a scratch harness (.local/m2m100-25locale-quality-test/, gitignored) reusing real production components (HugoParser, SegmentTranslator, the real 44-gate zero-defect WriteGateEvaluator, the real GATE36 fidelity judge) against two real source files: a title-only simple page (25/25 clean, 19/25 title text byte-identical to shipped LLM output) and a real complex technical blog post with code/tables/links (cells-spreadsheet-management-go: only 1/25 locales passed, mean fidelity ~0.28/1.0, 4/25 hard-crashed). CONCLUSION: do not route more locales to m2m100-alone-as-primary -- the evidence argues the opposite of the original ask; even the 3 CURRENT m2m100-primary locales (hu, ja) crashed outright on this real page and ro only scored a borderline 0.5/warn. TC-APT-006's original 40-segment content-free-proxy study substantially understated the real gap on complex content. Did NOT change model routing policy -- the mission's existing dual-model schema-enforced pairing (LLM as automatic retry/escalation on MT failure) already covers this; no policy change is evidence-supported. Instead, the assessment surfaced and fixed 3 concrete, previously-undocumented bugs: (1) b7ba0813 -- _translate_body_ast's AST-reuse map keyed by re-normalized placeholder-protected TEXT instead of stable node identity, causing two unrelated single-span units (e.g. a lone '.xlsx' code span and an unrelated footer link) to collide on the identical generic key '{PLACEHOLDER_0}' -- reproduced as a 100%-deterministic, locale-independent table-cell corruption (a 'Supported Formats' table's Extension column silently replaced with an unrelated blog link) across all 21 completed locales on the real test page. Fixed by keying on ASTNode.node_addr (already existed on TextUnit; added minimal SegmentContext.node_addr plumbing for body Segments) instead of re-derived text. Real GPU before/after repro confirms the table corruption is gone. (2) bfd20ddd -- a second, independent cause of the SAME frontmatter_segment_not_applied crash symptom: the placement-consistency check's expected-value snapshot predates TC-APT-042's legitimate cross-field-residual repair pass, which mutates a frontmatter unit's translated_text afterward -- causing a genuinely-fixed value to fail comparison against a stale pre-repair snapshot. Fixed by capturing the repair's actual rendered output (via the same accessor the check itself uses) into a new TranslationStats.fm_repair_overrides, merged into the expected-values set before the check runs -- widens acceptance ONLY for keys a repair actually touched, never weakening detection of a genuinely wrong translation. Real GPU before/after repro on hu and ja (2 of the mission's 3 current m2m100-primary locales) confirms both now complete with translate_error: None and sensible fully-translated frontmatter, where they previously hard-crashed on this exact page. (3) a604650f -- every MT backend (m2m100, nllb, opus, marian, small100) is fully deterministic (do_sample=False, fixed num_beams, never receives retry-feedback text), so campaign_runner.py's hard-coded 3 primary attempts before LLM escalation wasted 2 guaranteed-identical GPU generation cycles per failing cell for every m2m100-primary manifest. Fixed by collapsing the primary retry budget to 0 (exactly 1 real invocation) when the primary backend is deterministic, detected via the same registry `backend` field _llm_identity_gate already trusts -- an LLM-primary manifest (including the approved inverse pairing) is completely unaffected. All three fixes independently re-verified by the orchestrating session (not just trusted from the implementing agent) via re-run tests plus git-stash-confirmed pre-existing-failure baselines before each commit. TC-APT-107.note: Operator directive: validate m2m100+professionalize_llm split-model retry escalation across all 25 locales with real concurrent multi-process GPU usage on real aspose.org content, proactively finding/fixing gaps, before launching the full autonomous run across products/kb/docs/reference/blog.aspose.org. TC-APT-106 (3 bugs) closed this earlier. A full tests/unit/translation_engine/ regression sweep (task b3ncmt6j6, 1388 passed/6 failed/4 skipped) run to verify a 4th bug fix surfaced 3 more real, independent bugs, all now fixed: (a) commit 9260f0d8 -- ContentTypeRouter (segment-level ~line 1360 and unit-level ~line 2202 in segment_translator.py) assumed the model_loader-returned backend for its LLM model id always supports translate_with_context(), but the professionalize_llm circuit breaker can transparently substitute a non-context-capable MT fallback (e.g. m2m100_418m) without raising -- fixed by hasattr-guarding both sites and routing fallback-backed units through the existing MT translate paths instead of silent English passthrough. (b) commit f9b6f43d part 1 -- test_per_file_timeout.py/test_purity_backpressure.py opened config/global.yaml with a bare open() (platform-locale decode, cp1252 on this box) instead of encoding='utf-8' like every real production call site (src/utils/config_loader.py) already uses -- test-only bug, fixed. (c) commit f9b6f43d part 2 -- test_dropped_placeholder_fallback.py's _make_engine() left campaign_context as a bare MagicMock auto-attribute, which is truthy under .get(...), so _retry_dropped_placeholders_via_llm's defer_llm_fallbacks check always short-circuited before calling load_model(); real engines always set a genuine dict (engine_builder.py:134) so this never manifested in production -- test-only bug, fixed. All three verified via git-stash A/B (fail identically with the fix removed) plus full-suite reruns (27/27, 11/11, 4/4 respectively) with the fix applied. 2 failures remain OPEN, deliberately not patched this pass: test_content_type_router_frontmatter_wiring.py's test_routed_description_translation_reaches_final_translations_dict hits a real reconstruction-precedence question -- when the mocked _translate_body_ast doesn't run, translate_to_language() (segment_translator.py:1738, 'translated_frontmatter = doc.frontmatter') still treats doc.frontmatter as authoritative per TC-HT-004's 'AST is authoritative for frontmatter' invariant, so the segments-system ContentTypeRouter routing this test isolates never reaches the final result -- needs archaeology into whether Step 1b's segments-path routing is actually reachable in real (non-mocked) production traffic now that use_ast defaults true, or whether the test's premise is stale; risk of touching this without that is regressing the documented anti-overwrite fix at line 1736-1737. test_lang_detection_write_guard.py's test_keeps_untranslated_english_ordinary_prose_blocking: 'Deep Dive: The CSSOM in Python' against target 'it' strips to signal text 'Deep Dive: The in' (13 alpha chars), langdetect scores it en:0.714 -- below the 0.80 CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD -- so it silently passes as translated when it wasn't. Root cause is real (aggressive technical-token stripping degrades signal quality on short titles) but CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD was deliberately raised to 0.80 to fix 3 earlier false-positive incidents (TC-APT-040 x3, TC-APT-090, TC-APT-108) in this exact function -- lowering it risks reintroducing those. Needs a targeted fix (e.g. a distinct lower-confidence-but-still-actionable band), not a blanket threshold change.
